sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Marysville
sections.html:
A Marysville seller picks between an agent's listing, a private sale to someone found on your own, and a cash buyer who takes the place with its flaws. The real difference is how long each takes. A listing takes preparation, showings and a wait for a financed buyer's loan to clear, whereas cash can shorten the schedule when the house has deferred maintenance, a tenant or a looming deadline.

The city is now the second largest in Snohomish County, with an estimated 77,686 residents in July 2025, up 9.9 percent from the April 2020 base. Owners live in 69.4 percent of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $567,900, a mortgage holder pays about $2,409 a month, and typical gross rent is $1,997. Those are citywide figures, so use them as background only. Your price depends on your own house, its condition and recent sales on your street.

Whichever way you go, start by collecting:

  • The deed and your latest Snohomish County tax statement.
  • Payoff letters from your lender and any lienholder.
  • Receipts and permit records for big jobs such as a roof, addition or deck.
  • A completed seller disclosure statement.

Marysville is mostly a commuter city. Roughly 9 percent of residents work inside the city, about 20 percent in Everett and 13 percent in Seattle, and the mean trip is 31.5 minutes, with 70 percent driving alone. Community Transit runs four local routes plus express service from park and ride lots, including all-day trips to Lynnwood City Center station and peak service to the Boeing Everett Factory. The city sits outside the Sound Transit district.

Buyers pay attention to access to I-5 and State Route 529. Say plainly how long the drive is from your house to the on-ramp and to Everett.

sections.h2: Low ground, creeks and flood questions
sections.html: Downtown sits about 5 feet above sea level beside Ebey Slough, while eastern parts of town climb past 465 feet. Quilceda and Allen creeks drain the area. If your house is low or close to water, ask the county for the flood zone and get a survey in hand so a buyer's lender does not raise the issue first.

sections.h2: Permits, review times and ADU rules
sections.html:
Marysville posts how long staff review takes for each permit type. These are average calendar days for the first quarter of 2026.

Residential permit typeAverage review, days (Q1 2026)
Deck8
Demolition17
Remodel18
Addition20
New residential26
Accessory dwelling unit34

Submit applications in the online portal. Permit questions can go to MSVLPermits@marysvillewa.gov and planning questions to Planning@marysvillewa.gov. The phone line, 360-363-8000, is staffed from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Accessory dwelling units help on bigger lots. A lot may hold two, each at least 200 square feet and up to the greater of 1,000 square feet or 50 percent of the main house, capped at 1,400 square feet. Plan on one parking space per unit and, in most cases, separate water and sewer connections. Short-term rental units are prohibited in the city, so never pitch a house or ADU as a nightly rental.

The city publishes a zoning map. For property lines, a professional survey is the only reliable answer, and recorded surveys can be searched through the Snohomish County Auditor.

Two state rules drive most Marysville closings. Under RCW 64.06.020 the seller disclosure statement must reach the buyer five business days after both sides sign, unless they agree on a different timetable, and the buyer then holds a three business day right to back out. Excise tax is due at the moment of sale and is typically the seller's expense.

State rates climb in four bands, from 1.1 percent to 3 percent, and a local rate rides on top, so ask the Snohomish County Treasurer for the combined figure at your price. The first band ends at $551,000 for sales starting January 1, 2027 and at $525,000 before that. The city's median value of $567,900 puts a typical sale into the 1.28 percent band.

The assessor must value real property at 100 percent of true and fair market value, using a sales comparison, replacement cost or income approach. Each January 1 the county sets a fresh value, and the notice arrives in June. The following year's tax is built on it.

Doubt the number? Call the assessor's line printed on the notice and ask for an appraiser. If the answer is unsatisfying, petition the Board of Equalization, using whichever of two cutoffs comes later: 60 days after the mailing or July 1. Questions about that go to 425-388-3407. The tax itself is split into April 30 and October 31 installments, and a postmark on mail is enough. Escrow prorates the current bill at closing.

Your sequence is short. Sign the accepted offer, then deliver the disclosure inside the five business day window. Let the title company set the closing date and prepare a settlement statement showing payoff and excise tax. Hand over keys when funds are released.

With a cash buyer there is no loan approval to wait for and little inspection haggling. A listing keeps both, so it runs longer but can fetch more for a house in good shape.

sections.h2: What the buyer will see on a Marysville lot
sections.html:
Marysville runs north to south along Interstate 5, with the Tulalip reservation to the west and State Route 9 to the east. Parts of the city sit in the Arlington, Lake Stevens or Lakewood school districts, though the Marysville School District covers most of it, so a buyer with children should confirm the district for your exact address. A buyer will also ask who supplies what at the house and whether there are open permits, so settle both before you list.

Newer subdivisions and older neighborhoods trade at different prices, and a nearby sale of a similar house tells you more than the citywide median does. Ask an agent or a cash buyer which recent sales they used and how they adjusted for condition.

Look at what lands in your account. Take the offer, subtract the payoff and excise tax, and set the result beside a list-price scenario after commission, repair credits and the months of payments you would carry. Get the closing date in writing and run the transfer through a title company.

faqs.q: How long does a Marysville permit take to review?
faqs.a: It varies by type. First quarter 2026 averages were 8 days for decks, 18 for remodels, 26 for new residential and 34 for accessory dwelling units, counted as calendar days of staff review. Revisions can add time.

faqs.q: Can I use a Marysville ADU as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: No. Short-term rental units are currently prohibited in Marysville, so a buyer planning nightly rentals would need another plan.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my Snohomish County assessed value?
faqs.a: Use whichever date is later: 60 days after the notice was mailed or July 1. The petition goes to the Board of Equalization, and the clerk answers questions at 425-388-3407. An attorney is optional. Evidence that the value is wrong is not.

faqs.q: Who pays the Washington excise tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: Typically the seller. The county treasurer collects it as of the sale date, and a closing agent ordinarily subtracts it from what you receive. If a seller leaves it unpaid, the obligation can shift to the buyer.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a Marysville buyer a disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Usually yes, for improved residential property. RCW 64.06.020 prescribes the form and a five business day delivery window, after which the buyer has three business days to rescind. A written waiver or an exempt transfer changes that.
